items.title: Smooth and Sobolev configuration and reduced gauge spaces
items.statement: Fix compact connected oriented boundaryless smooth Riemannian M, d=3 or4, N>=2, smooth principal SU(N) bundle P and smooth reference A0. Define A_k=A0+H^k(T*M tensor adP), integer k>d/2+1, G_{k+1}=H^{k+1} sections of AdP, Gbar=G/Z_N, based G_m={u:u(p_m)=e}, A_infty=A0+Omega^1(adP) with seminorm C-infty topology, and smooth gauge group with C-infty section topology. Quotients have quotient topology. Define irreducible as holonomy acts irreducibly on C^N; do not replace this by full holonomy without proof. Fix action A^u=u^-1Au+u^-1du and Sobolev norms by a finite bundle atlas.
items.local_proof_obligation: Specify all spaces, norm equivalence, basepoint frame and finite central quotient; locally define any unprovided adjoint-bundle/Sobolev-section conventions. Definition only; smoothness claims in the next lemma.

items.title: Sobolev gauge calculus and smooth gauge action
items.statement: For data of the preceding definition, finite-atlas Sobolev norms are equivalent; H^k sections embed in C1 for k>d/2+1, pointwise multiplication H^k x H^k→H^k is bounded, local matrix exponential/log charts make G_{k+1} a Hilbert Lie group, and the gauge action A_k x G_{k+1}→A_k is smooth.
items.local_proof_obligation: Transfer existing Euclidean-domain product/embedding estimates with cutoffs; construct section charts explicitly. Prove Nemytskii derivatives and one-derivative loss, not just scalar product boundedness. Constants are uniform over the fixed finite atlas.

items.title: Gauge stabilizers and properness of the Sobolev action
items.statement: For the compact connected base and regularity above, evaluation identifies the stabilizer at A with the centralizer of Hol_A in SU(N); irreducible A has stabilizer Z_N. If A_j→A and A_j^{u_j}→B in H^k, then a subsequence u_j converges in H^{k+1}. Consequently the action of Gbar_{k+1} on A_k^* is free and proper.
items.source_locator: Singer p8–9 stabilizers; NR Lemmas2.2,2.5–2.8 and Prop2.4, pp124–125
items.local_proof_obligation: Use parallel-transport ODE and compactness at one fibre for a uniform-convergent subsequence, then bootstrap d u=u B-A u in Sobolev norms. Supply finite-atlas proof for arbitrary smooth P/SU(N), not merely cite NR S3/SU2. Apply the inspected complex-unitary Schur statement to the holonomy representation, whose operators are bounded in finite dimension; determinant one reduces unit scalars to Z_N.

items.title: Rough-coefficient covariant Green inverse and Coulomb splitting
items.statement: For A in A_k^*, d_A^*d_A:H^{k+1}(adP)→H^{k-1}(adP) is an isomorphism with bounded inverse G_A, and H^k(T*M tensor adP)=im d_A direct-sum ker d_A^*. The bounded projection onto im d_A is d_A G_A d_A^*. The inverse and projections depend smoothly on A near each irreducible A.
items.local_proof_obligation: Smooth-coefficient imported Green theorem does NOT directly cover Sobolev A. Derive distributional bootstrapping and a priori estimate from a fixed smooth reference operator plus product bounds; prove closed range/cokernel/kernel assertions and continuity of inverses. Do not use based point condition as if d_A^*d_A were surjective on its point-vanishing subspace.

items.title: Sobolev and smooth irreducible gauge-orbit principal bundles
items.statement: A_k^* is open and A_k^*→A_k^*/Gbar_{k+1} is a locally trivial smooth principal Gbar_{k+1} bundle. At A, a sufficiently small ball in A+ker d_A^* is a slice, with no intersections between different reduced-group translates; saturation is open and the orbit quotient is Hausdorff. The corresponding C-infty irreducible projection is a locally trivial topological principal Gbar_infty bundle with the actual C-infty quotient topology.
items.source_locator: Singer Thm1 p9; Mitter Prop4.4 and5.6, Thm5.28–5.29 pp467–472; NR §4
items.local_proof_obligation: At (A,e), D(a,xi)=a+d_A xi is bounded iso by splitting. Banach IFT gives only near-identity uniqueness; use properness to exclude far gauge returns to a sufficiently small slice. Prove regularity/uniqueness compatibility over k to obtain C-infty local sections and continuity in every seminorm. An inverse-limit assertion alone is insufficient.

items.title: Central stabilizer and based stabilizer comparison
items.statement: For a smooth connection over connected M, a gauge transformation preserving A is determined by one fibre value; basepoint identity forces it to be identity. For irreducible SU(N) connections full stabilizer is Z_N, and the reduced action is free.

items.title: Finite holonomy witnesses for irreducibility
items.statement: For smooth connections on principal SU(N) bundles over M=S3 orS4, irreducibility is witnessed by finitely many based piecewise-smooth loop holonomies having no common proper complex invariant subspace. Such a finite tuple remains irreducible under sufficiently small connection perturbations in C1; hence A_infty^* is open.
items.local_proof_obligation: Use compactness of the finite union of complex Grassmannians to extract a finite holonomy witness and continuity of parallel transport. Do not identify irreducibility with Hol_A=SU(N) for N>2. Supply the finite-dimensional Grassmannian compactness argument locally or exact earlier supplier.

items.title: Relative finite-parameter avoidance of reducible connections
items.statement: For fixed smooth principal SU(N) P over S3 orS4, every continuous map f:K→A_infty from a finite polyhedron K with f(L)⊂A_infty^* on a subpolyhedron L is homotopic relative L to a map into A_infty^*. The homotopy can be chosen arbitrarily small in any specified C-infty neighborhood of f, after retaining an irreducible neighborhood of L.
items.local_proof_obligation: Author the concrete finite-holonomy proof in constructive_avoidance_argument below. No infinite-dimensional stratification theorem is assumed. All loop-control, finite-dimensional incidence and relative collar details are required.
items.proof_status: established-target; constructive finite-holonomy proof route independently assessed; carrier not yet authored

constructive_avoidance_argument: For a compact irreducible boundary/collar family, compactness of each complex Grassmannian and then compactness of parameter space gives finitely many loops whose joint holonomies have no invariant proper subspace uniformly there. When N>2 this is representation irreducibility, not full SU(N) holonomy.

Replace chosen piecewise-smooth loops by sufficiently close loops with pairwise disjoint small control arcs, each unused by all other loops; use dimension3/4 room and local detours, keeping based endpoints fixed. Uniform continuity of holonomy on the compact connection family preserves the boundary irreducibility margin. Add arbitrarily many further loops with their own control arcs. This geometric construction must be explicit.

Smooth the finite-dimensional parameter dependence of the affine disk extension only in its interior, retaining a collar on which all connections remain irreducible. Use finite partition-of-unity approximation in the locally convex space of smooth1-forms; retain the original boundary family exactly. The relative approximation is a proof obligation; ordinary target-manifold smoothing alone is insufficient.

For each loop, use bump1-forms supported in its control tube. The standard ODE variation formula for parallel transport identifies derivative of its holonomy with the integral of the transported contraction of the perturbing1-form. Choosing those forms with transported Lie-algebra bases makes the derivative in r dimSU(N) real parameters surjective, while the other loops are unaffected. Coefficients may depend smoothly on the interior disk parameter. Prove the resulting connection family is jointly smooth there and continuous into C-infty at the collar.

Let I_k={(g1,...,gr,V):V∈Gr_C(k,N),g_i V=V}. It is a smooth bundle over Gr_C(k,N) with fibre H_k^r, H_k=S(U(k)×U(N-k)). Its dimension is 2k(N-k)+r(dimSU(N)−2k(N-k)), hence deficit 2(r−1)k(N-k) in SU(N)^r. Its projection image need not be a submanifold; use the incidence manifold itself.

For joint holonomy F(s,v) submersive in v, W_k={(s,v,V):(F(s,v),V)∈I_k} is a finite-dimensional manifold by transversality to the incidence condition; dimension=dim(s)+dim(v)−2(r−1)k(N-k). Choose r so the deficit exceeds disk parameter dimension for every1≤k<N. Then projection W_k→v has everywhere critical image of measurezero by Sard; countable charts and finitely many k suffice. Choose arbitrarily small v outside these images.

Multiply perturbations by a cutoff zero on the fixed boundary collar and positive on the region requiring repair. Where cutoff is positive, normalized v derivative remains uniformly invertible for all sufficiently small v by the compact-family ODE estimates; where it vanishes irreducibility was retained already. The Sard argument applies on the open interior support, and the collar remains fixed. Straight interpolation of small perturbations gives the required relative homotopy; no irreducibility is claimed at intermediate homotopy times away from L.

For general finite polyhedron use finitely many simplices and relative finite-skeleton extension; disk/sphere cases suffice for the weak-contractibility theorem. Prove the compatibility instead of treating a nonsmooth polyhedron as a smooth manifold.

items.title: Weak contractibility of the irreducible connection locus
items.statement: For every smooth principal SU(N) P over S3 orS4, N>=2, A_infty^* is nonempty and path-connected and pi_j(A_infty^*,A)=0 for every j>=1 and A in A_infty^*.

items.statement: For any smooth principal SU(N) P over S^r, r=3 or4, evaluate at chosen p_m. Then G_m→G→SU(N) is a locally trivial fibre bundle, and G→Gbar=G/Z_N is a finite covering. These are fibrations to which the imported homotopy LES applies.

items.title: Low special-unitary homotopy needed for the global obstruction
items.statement: For N>=2, pi_1 SU(N)=pi_2 SU(N)=0 and pi_3 SU(N)=Z. For SU2≅S3, pi_4(S3) is finite and pi_5(S3) is nonzero.
items.source_locator: Singer p10 proof ofTheorem3 and p11 proof ofTheorem7 (pi_{4+j}(S3)=Z2 for j=0,1); Toda reference[8]
items.local_proof_obligation: Construct SU(N-1)→SU(N)→S^{2N-1} as a locally trivial bundle and prove pi1/pi2 vanishing and pi3=Z by the imported fibration LES and sphere connectivity/degree. Prove the genuinely necessary unstable inputs: pi4(S3) finite and pi5(S3) nonzero. The standard stronger computations pi4(S3)=pi5(S3)=Z2 suffice if their actual proofs are reconstructed, but no stronger numerical computation is required. items.title: Nontrivial homotopy of reduced sphere gauge groups
items.statement: For r=3 or4, N>=2 and every smooth SU(N) P→S^r, Gbar(P) has at least one nontrivial homotopy group or more than one path component.
items.source_locator: Singer Theorems3,5 pp9–10 and Theorem7 proof p11; local smaller numerical route through SU(N) sphere fibrations, independently checked
items.local_proof_obligation: For S3, pi0G=pi3SU(N)=Z and finite-center quotient changes components by only a finite image, leaving infinitely many. For S4 and N>=2, evaluation LES gives injection pi1G_m=pi5SU(N)→pi1G since pi2SU(N)=0; the finite covering injects pi1G→pi1Gbar. For N=2 use pi5(S3)≠0. For N=3, the SU2→SU3→S5 LES gives image[pi5SU3→pi5S5=Z]=kernel[Z→pi4SU2]; this kernel contains a nonzero integer since pi4SU2 is finite, hence pi5SU3≠0. For N>=4, SU(N-1)→SU(N)→S^{2N-1} stabilizes pi5 because pi5 and pi6 of those spheres vanish by dimension/connectivity. Never assume the map Z→pi4SU2 surjects, or that finite center preserves pi0; odd SU2 bundle sector can have connected Gbar. State all maps and basepoints.

existing_target.statement: Let N>=2, M=S4 (also S3), and P→M be any fixed smooth principal SU(N) bundle. Give the affine smooth connection space A and smooth gauge group G their C-infty section topologies and A/G its quotient topology. The orbit projection A→A/G has no continuous right inverse. Indeed its restriction A*→A*/(G/Z_N) to connections with irreducible holonomy representation has no continuous section.
existing_target.proof_obligation: A global section restricts to the saturated irreducible locus; e supplies the principal reduced bundle, h weak contractibility, m nontrivial reduced-group homotopy, and n gives contradiction. Include all bundle sectors and N>=2. Source statement also announces extension to compact connected semisimple groups; any broader approved group class must retain a separate central-cover/simple-factor reduction proof obligation before being claimed.
